concerns.text: Task T000 permits a 'Sim-Baseline' fallback if real hardware is unavailable. This silently relaxes FR-004 and US-2 which mandate execution in the 'real-world environment' to validate the sim-to-real bridge. Generating synthetic/simulated baseline data invalidates the primary hypothesis test (SC-001) and violates Constitution Principle VI (Simulation Fidelity Independence) which forbids using simulation for primary metrics.

Task T037 implements the 'Perfect Low-Level Executor' (Oracle) using 'high-fidelity simulation with ground-truth physics'. This violates Constitution Principle VI (Simulation Fidelity Independence) which states that performance metrics MUST be derived from real-world execution, not the simulation layer. The Oracle is a diagnostic tool; using it to generate success rates for the 'Physics Fidelity Gap' (SC-006) conflates simulation fidelity with the symbolic abstraction hypothesis.

Task T036 defines 'catastrophic failure' to include 'Controller Execution Failure when caused by unmodeled dynamics'. SC-005 defines catastrophic failure as 'complete task abandonment due to unmodeled dynamics'. The task requires a causal inference engine to distinguish 'unmodeled dynamics' from simple hardware glitches, a capability not defined in FR-006 or the spec. This makes the acceptance criterion (≤ 5% threshold) untestable and the task a semantic weakening of the requirement.

Task T041 calculates the 'Physics Fidelity Gap' using the Oracle success rate derived from simulation (per T037). SC-006 and US-4 define this gap as the difference between the *theoretical* planner capability and *real-world* execution. Since T037 uses simulation, the calculated gap measures 'Simulation vs Real' rather than 'Planner vs Controller', misinterpreting the successcriterion and violating the isolation control logic required by the spec.

Task T003 forbids falling back to synthetic data but fails to include a mechanism to *verify* the 'verified real source' integrity (checksums) before processing. This violates Constitution Principle III (Data Hygiene) and Principle I (Reproducibility
